question: Normally, in a healthy adult, the initial filtrate in the kidneys is about _________ daily.
solution:
The correct answer is __**180 L**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The initial filtrate in the kidneys of a healthy adult is about **180 liters daily**.
 
• This filtrate consists of water, glucose, salts, and waste products from the blood.
 
• Approximately **99% of this filtrate is reabsorbed** back into the bloodstream.
 
• The remaining 1% forms urine, which is excreted from the body.
 
• This process is crucial for maintaining the body's fluid and electrolyte balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nephron**

 
 
• The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney responsible for the formation of urine.
 
• Each kidney contains about 1 million nephrons.
 
• Nephrons filter blood, reabsorb needed substances, and excrete waste as urine.
 
 
 
• **Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)**
 
 
• GFR is the rate at which the blood is filtered in the kidneys.
 
• It is a measure of kidney function, with a normal GFR being around 90-120 mL/min.
 
• Decreased GFR may indicate kidney disease.
 
 
 
• **Reabsorption in Kidneys**
 
 
• Reabsorption involves the movement of water and solutes back into the bloodstream.
 
• It primarily occurs in the renal tubules of the nephron.
 
• Essential substances like glucose, amino acids, and ions are selectively reabsorbed.
 
 
 
• **Urine Formation**
 
 
• Urine formation involves three main processes: filtration, reabsorption, and secretion.
 
• The final urine is composed of water, urea, creatinine, and other waste products.
 
• On average, a healthy adult excretes about 1-2 liters of urine daily.
